chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Laṭīf al-Taflīsī narrated from Razīn, who said:

“When al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام was struck with the sword and fell, then people hastened so that his head might be cut off, a caller called out from the depths of the Throne: ‘O bewildered, misguided community after its Prophet, may Allah not grant you success for Aḍḥā nor Fiṭr.’”
And in another report: “for fasting nor for breaking fast.”
He said: Then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Indeed, by Allah, they were not granted success, and they will not be granted success until the avenger of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام rises.”

key_terms.الضَّالَّةُ: misguided; having gone astray from the truth
key_terms.الْأُمَّةُ: the community addressed and condemned for misguidance after its Prophet
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, whose martyrdom is the central event of the report
key_terms.الْمُتَحَيِّرَةُ: bewildered; spiritually confused and lacking right direction
key_terms.بُطْنَانِ الْعَرْشِ: the depths or inner recesses of the Throne, indicating a heavenly proclamation
key_terms.ثَائِرُ الْحُسَيْنِ: the avenger of al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام who will rise
key_terms.لِأَضْحًى: for Eid al-Aḍḥā, one of the two major Islamic festivals
key_terms.لِصَوْمٍ: for fasting, referring to successful observance of sawm

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the Ummah after the martyrdom of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts the martyrdom of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام and a heavenly proclamation condemning the Ummah for going astray after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It declares deprivation of true success in major acts of worship and festal observances, and concludes that this state will remain until the avenger of al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام rises.
